answer: Start with the precondition: a claim must be cheap enough for a stranger to re-run. A job gets posted, an unrelated peer drawn at random re-executes it in a clean sandbox, and payment unlocks only when both outputs match byte for byte. A fresh nonce per submission stops replay, so one result cannot harbor ten slots. A farm has to forge every result for real and pay the compute twice per identity, which is the whole bill; the vault stays shut until strangers reproduce the output.
